answers.strategy:
Mostly check for forced moves; consider the amount of unclear blocks against the number of blocks a hint gives you info for. For example 5 2 1 is a forced config because you have 5 + 2 + 1 which is 8 solid blocks with 2 guaranteed gaps, which tells you this is a 10 block hint which is your forced move on an opener.

If you click a block due to this forced move that is the edge of a row/column, you can then extend off of that block given those row/column's corresponding hints.

When you have a 4 block guaranteed to be within a 7 block span, and you have 1 block placed already, you know that some neighbours of that block is guaranteed due to limited space.

Right clicking guaranteed non-usable spaces helped.

I also used the meta gaming of the hint button to my advantage as a "debugger" to check if I placed anything incorrectly so far; I would imagine someone can use it as a gamble check, but I didn't want to use it because of the disaster situation which happened to me in game 3.
